analysis: Aspirin causes platelet dysfunction by inhibiting the cyclooxygenase enzyme, which reduces thromboxane A2 production and impairs platelet aggregation. This increases the risk of bleeding, particularly in patients already on heparin, which also acts as an anticoagulant by enhancing the activity of antithrombin III. The combination of these two drugs can significantly increase the risk of bleeding due to their complementary effects on different parts of the clotting cascade.
